changes.headline: G7 confirms 100 Mbbl IEA-coordinated release
changes.dek: Up to 100 Mbbl over 4 months (~50 diesel + ~50 crude), diesel front-loaded into first 20 days, begins immediately. The G7, meeting by video under the French chairmanship on Friday, agreed to a coordinated IEA release of up to 100 million barrels of emergency stocks over four months, beginning immediately: roughly 50 million barrels of diesel from European stocks plus 50 million barrels of crude from IEA members, with a 'frontloaded substantial diesel release' inside the first 20 days. The G7 also reaffirmed no export bans on energy products and coordinated refinery maintenance schedules. 100 Mbbl is about a day of global demand spread over four months: real relief for the tightest product market, but policy supply, not barrels found.
changes.balance_read: The release is the ceiling on the product market; the physical drivers (Russia's diesel export ban through Oct 31, China's October product-export halt) are the floor. The first 20 days of front-loaded diesel run straight into the Russian ban's Oct 31 expiry.
changes.publishers: G7 leaders' statement on energy security, via AP

changes.headline: Friday's panic unwound into the close
changes.dek: WTI settled $91.11 (-1.9%); Dec Brent $102.25 (-0.06%), essentially flat; mid-session lows were ~$89.50 / ~$99.90. Friday's full settled session reads differently from the mid-session panic: WTI settled $91.11 (-$1.76, -1.9%) and December Brent $102.25 (-$0.06, -0.06%), essentially unchanged after Thursday's $102.31 close. For the week: Brent +0.11%, WTI -1.6%. Brent kept the $100 handle it spent three sessions under earlier in the week. Futures are closed at digest time Sunday (Globex reopens 16:00 MDT Sunday); the tape is Friday's settled session.
changes.balance_read: Flat price trades escalation optionality, not missing barrels (Gulf exports 98% of pre-war, Hormuz at pre-war rates): Friday showed how fast that optionality reprices on a policy headline.

changes.headline: WCS front widens into the recovery, three sessions running
changes.dek: TMW Nov26 -$24.13 (-$0.38); Dec26 -$24.65 (-$0.40, widest on strip); WCS Nov outright ~$66.98. TMW (ICE WCS 1A) EOD Oct 2: Nov26 -$24.13 (-$0.38), Dec26 -$24.65 (-$0.40, widest tenor on the strip), Jan27 -$23.30 down the strip to Oct27 -$17.20; the whole strip sold off $0.1-0.7. Three straight sessions of front widening: Thursday into the crude rally, Friday into the selloff, and Friday's settle holds the move while flat price recovered into the close. WCS Nov outright ~$66.98 (WTI settled $91.11 minus TMW -$24.1311), down ~$2.1 from Thursday, with the differential doing the damage. Cross-grades: ARV Nov26 -$14.86 (-$0.31), ARV-TMW arb +$9.28 (from +$9.21): the constraint sits at the egress end. TMU +$3.40; TMF +$3.85 holding into diluent season; TMS +$5.98, SYN-WCS $30.11.
changes.balance_read: A diesel release does not add a single barrel of egress at Kerrobert. The diff trades the November-December egress crunch; flat price trades the war. They are different markets now.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center end-of-day settlements, Oct 2, 2026 (all six contracts)

changes.headline: Diesel $100+ regime breaks at $97.94
changes.dek: NYMEX diesel crack $97.94 (Oct 2): first sub-$100 close after eighteen straight above; 3-2-1 $64.65. The NYMEX diesel crack closed at $97.94 on Oct 2, the first sub-$100 close after eighteen straight days above $100. Not a record: all-time maximum $117.92 (Sep 16). 28 total $100+ closes in the 2020+ history; the first sustained regime began 2026-08-17. The 3-2-1 crack stands at $64.65 against a $75.31 maximum (Aug 28). The break came with the G7 release going concrete: policy supply landing directly on the tightest product market, while Russia's diesel export ban (through Oct 31) and China's October product-export cancellations keep the physical drivers in place.
changes.balance_read: Crude flow and product availability are not the same market; Friday proved it in reverse, with gasoil (-5% mid-session) moving twice as hard as crude.
changes.publishers: Validated crack history (Yahoo front-month futures), refreshed Oct 4, 2026

changes.headline: Hormuz strike cadence: three straight days
changes.dek: Sunday: tanker struck with engine-room damage; Friday: two tankers; Thursday: one tanker. UKMTO reports a tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday with damage to its engine room (Reuters, 13:22 IST); crew safe, no environmental impact. That extends the cadence to three straight days: Thursday (tanker hit, fire), Friday (two tankers, one exiting the strait with a small fire and blackout, one east of Oman), Sunday (engine-room damage). Flow data still says the physical market is intact: Gulf exports 98% of pre-war (JPMorgan), Hormuz at pre-war rates on the seven-day average (Kpler), Saudi East-West pipeline restarted Sep 29.
changes.balance_read: Ships struck daily, barrels flowing at 98%. The market prices the trajectory (escalation risk vs. the ceasefire track), not the body count.
changes.publishers: UKMTO incident reports via Reuters, Oct 1-4, 2026

changes.headline: Egress watch: November notice is the next observation
changes.dek: Oct apportionment 8%/4% at Kerrobert; November notice ~mid-October. October Mainline apportionment at Kerrobert stands at 8% on lights and 4% on heavies (Enbridge official notice, Sep 16). The November notice lands around mid-October and decides whether the binding-from-November base case is right. Trans Mountain's drag-reducing-agent project adds about 90 kb/d in service January 2027: a January event, no relief for a fourth-quarter 2026 crunch. The Sep 28 toll settlement moves TMX firm contracted capacity from 80% to 90% effective Jan 1, 2027. Pacific Link designated Oct 1 as the first project of national interest under the Building Canada Act (~1 Mb/d, $35.2-43.7B, conditions by Sep 1, 2027): long-dated, prompt-neutral. In-house allocator base case: Mainline binding from November, Keystone and TMX at 100%, max modeled congestion rent $8.65/bbl (modeled, not observed).
changes.balance_read: Long-dated projects change the 2028+ math; the November-December crunch trades on the apportionment notice.
changes.publishers: Enbridge notice (Sep 16); Trans Mountain CER application (Sep 2026)
